chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a man, between me and him was a relationship, who died and left young children, and left slaves for him, boys and girls, and did not make a bequest. So what is your view regarding the one who buys the slave girl from them to serve as the mother of his child, and what is your view regarding their sale? He said: 'If there is a guardian for them who manages their affairs, sells them on their behalf, and looks out for their interests, he is rewarded in doing so.' I said, 'So what is your view regarding the one who buys the slave girl from them, so he takes her as the mother of his child?' He said: 'There is no problem with that, if that evaluation is established for them by the supervisor with regards to what is correct for them, and there is not for them to retract with regards to what the supervisor establishes for them with regards to what is right for them.'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a child (a female slave who bears her master's child)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling slave children left by an intestate father, and can a buyer take one as a mother of a child?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of intestate succession regarding slave children, emphasizing the guardian's (wali) fiduciary duty to act in their best interest during the sale of their personhood. It specifically validates the status of 'Umm Walad' acquired through such a sale, establishing that the children cannot later contest the transaction once the guardian has executed it properly, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the finality of the wali's administrative decisions in estate management.
